Claims 1-6 and 8-16 are pending in this application upon entry of this
amendment, with claim 1 being an independent claim. The various parts of the Office Action (and other matters, if any) are discussed below under appropriate headings.
I. CLAIM OBJECTIONS
The Examiner objects to claims 1 and 2 are objected to because of informalities. The claims have been amended to address the informalities. Withdrawal of the objection is respectfully requested.
II. CLAIM REJECTIONS - 35 U.S.C. § 101
Applicant asks the Examiner to reconsider and withdraw the rejection of the

claims based on 35 U.S.C. § 101. More particularly, the Examiner asserts nothing in the identified limitations preclude features as recited in previously presented independent claim 1 from being performed in the mind. While it is not conceded that the recited features found in the claims can be fairly characterized as mental processes, it is submitted that independent claim 1 has been amended to recite additional features that cannot be characterized as abstract. For instance, claim 1 (as amended) recites:
the noise waveform from the response signal (SResponse).

Such features are representatively depicted in paragraphs [0051], [0072], and [0074] and FIG. 4 of the published application, reproduced below. As described in the current application, the anesthetizing monitoring unit 110 includes one or more transceivers 104 and processing circuitry 103 with the processor 102 and the memory 106. The processing circuitry 103 is communicatively coupled to the measurement

III. CLAIM REJECTIONS - 35 U.S.C. § 102

Applicant asks the Examiner to reconsider and withdraw the rejection of the claims based on Kurtz et al., U.S. 20170245776 (Kurtz). Independent claim 1 is amended to clarify that the noise signal is gathered outside of when the stimuli signal is sent or the response signal is received:
transmitting a single stimuli signal (Sstimuii) using an output port of
the anesthetizing monitoring unit,
receiving an a single evoked electromyography, EMG, response
signal (SResponse), having a duration (TResponse), in response to the
transmitted stimuli signal (Sstimuii) using an input port of the anesthetizing
monitoring unit,
estimating a periodic noise waveform (SPeriodic), having the duration
(TResponse), by using temporal segments of a noise signal (SNoise)

Such features are representatively depicted in FIGS. 2A and 2B of the published application, reproduced below. The stimuli signal (Sstimuli) comprises a single pulse, such as a pulse of a pulse wave or a pulse and a single evoked electromyography, EMG. The response signal (SResponse) is received by the anesthetizing monitoring unit 110 in response to the stimuli signal (Sstimuii).

The method further includes an adjacent time interval (TNoise) that excludes or does not overlap with the stimuli signal interval (Tstimuius) and/or the response signal interval (TResponse). The noise signal (SNoise) Is detected and/or obtained during the adjacent time interval (TNoise). The detected noise signal (SNoise) is then split into a number of temporal segments and the periodic noise template (STemplate) is generated by aggregating the temporal segments. A periodic noise waveform (SPeriodic) is estimated using the temporal segments of the detected noise signal (SNoise) and the improved

Thus, the anesthetizing monitoring unit 110 has the advantage of adapting to time invariant noise, as a noise estimate may be generated for each stimuli/response. This is especially a problem as the response signal amplitude diminishes with the application of drugs. In one example, the periodic noise can appear as an interfering signal such that the current amplitude of the response signal appears as a current pulse response corrupted by varying or non-constant amplitude.

The method and device of Kurtz is configured differently. The method of Kurtz involves generating a plurality of stimuli, receiving a noisy signal related to evoked response to the plurality of stimuli, and dividing the noisy signal into a plurality of responses to the plurality of stimuli. A static matrix is estimated for the plurality of responses, shrink the static matrix, calculate weights based on an inverse of the shrunk statistic matrix, and applying the weights to the plurality of responses to construct a final response.

Because Kurtz involves sending out a plurality of stimuli and receiving a plurality of responses, Kurtz does not teach or suggest "transmitting a single stimuli signal (Sstimui) using an output port of the anesthetizing monitoring unit, receiving an a sinqe evoked electromyography, EMG, response signal (SResponse), having a duration (TResponse), in response to the transmitted stimuli signal (Sstimuli) using an input port of the anesthetizing monitoring unit, estimating a periodic noise waveform (SPeriodic), having the duration (TResponse), by using temporal segments of a noise signal (SNoise)."

In view of the above, Kurtz does not disclose or suggest the features as recited in amended independent claim 1. Accordingly, independent claim 1 is patentable over Kurtz, and the dependent claims are patentable for at least the same reasons.

IV. NEW CLAIMS
Newly-added claims 15 and 16 depend from base independent claim 1, and are patentable for at least the reasons given above for the patentability of independent claim 1 as amended.
Additionally, Kurtz does teach or suggest the features of claim 15. Claim 15

includes the feature that "the threshold values are predetermined properties of historical improved response signals received at the anesthetizing monitoring unit prior to the response signal (SResponse) being received by the anesthetizing monitoring unit, wherein the threshold values are stored in the memory of the anesthetizing monitoring unit." The Examiner asserts that paragraph [0135] of Kurtz discloses the claim feature of thresholds, as recited in claim 6.

Paragraph [0135] of Kurtz describes a mismatch negativity (MMN) response that determined when the peak amplitude of a processed deviant response is statistically different than that of a standard response in the region of expected MMN, which is between 50 and 300 ms after onset of stimulus. As noted in Kurtz, as the MMN response depends on the consciousness state of the subject, in the awake pre-op state, there should be a significant MMN, while in the anesthesia state, there should not be an MMN present. Thus, there is no indication in Kurtz that the threshold values are based on properties of historical improved response signals. Accordingly, for at least the reasons above, Kurtz does not disclose or suggest the features as recited in new claim 15.
